transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because... most days I just wake up already feeling like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting on me. And it just doesn't lift. Even when I'm out working with the crew, or at home around my kids, I just can't seem to shake it. It's this constant low, hollow feeling, like I'm really just going through the motions every day.
How long have you been feeling this way, on and off, over the last few years?

I'd say it's been going on for about three years and three months now. It started right around the time the groundskeeping contract changed at work. They messed with our schedule, and... well, the longer days just kind of took over my life. I've been feeling this way pretty much ever since.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a chronic, low-level depressive state lasting over two years (specifically 3 years and 3 months), which is the hallmark of Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia). Given the chronicity and lack of reported episodic severity, F34.1 is the most appropriate diagnosis, allowing me to rule out F32.9 and F33.9.
